title: search.query
description: Run a search from a server-side caller. The payload is the same parameter set GET /search/api/v1/query accepts (type, q, lang, category, f.<slug>, r.<slug>, lat/lon/radius_km or bbox, geo_mode, qu, sort, facets, limit, anchor, direction) and the answer is the same envelope: {items, facets, facet_meta, next_anchor, prev_anchor, has_next, has_prev, count, count_is_lower_bound, exact_total, degraded, backend, sort, took_ms}, plus `bands` under geo_mode=rank and `query_understanding` when extraction ran. `count` is ALWAYS the whole matching total, never the nearby count. `count` is nullable and is NEVER 0 beside a non-empty items[]: `count_is_lower_bound` marks a floor (render 'N+'), `null` means the engine cannot say (render no count). Every item carries `promoted` (DSA Art. 26) under every sort, including when it is false. Geo answers obey `audience`: the default `anonymous` measures them against the ~1.1km public grid a card publishes, and `distance_km` comes back floored to that grid's cell diagonal.

type.description: Registered doc_type; one type per query (no federated search in v1).

q.description: Free text; dictionary-normalized, morphology is the engine's.

lang.description: Language code selecting the FTS config and dictionary.

anchor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous answer.

radius_km.description: Distance around the centre in km. Its MEANING is geo_mode's: under `rank` it is the edge of the `nearby` band and excludes nothing; under `filter` it is a hard cut. Defaults to NEAR_BAND_RADIUS_KM (25) under `rank`.

bbox.description: minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon; minLon > maxLon crosses the antimeridian. For an anonymous audience the rectangle is grown OUTWARD to whole ~1.1km cells of the public geo grid: a box EXCLUDES rows, so halving one around a listing would otherwise converge on the seller's pin in a few dozen requests.

audience.description: WHO the answer is for, on stapel-attributes' visibility axis. Defaults to `anonymous`, which measures every geo answer against the ~1.1km public grid a card publishes: `distance_km` is floored to that grid's cell diagonal (~1.574km), `bbox` is snapped to whole cells, and `radius_km` / `sort=distance` / the `nearby` band read the grid point rather than the stored one. Pass `owner` or `staff` — per call, deliberately — when the caller is the listing's own seller or an internal tool that needs the exact position. The transport cannot infer it, and a transport that guessed would be the side door around the gate.

geo_mode.description: What radius_km means. `rank` PARTITIONS the answer around lat/lon: `nearby` (inside radius_km) first, then `all` carrying every remaining row — including rows with no coordinates. Nothing is withheld by distance, `count` stays the whole matching total, and a query cannot come back empty because of geo. Each item gains `band`; the answer gains `bands[]` of {id, count, radius_km?}. `filter` is the historical hard cut, for a caller that genuinely wants only what is within N km — a deliberate act, never injected. `rank` is the default inside the feature; while STAPEL_SEARCH['GEO_BANDS'] is off this parameter is inert and radius_km filters as it always has. Without lat/lon, ranking is simply inactive, which is not an error.

qu.description: Query understanding. `auto` (default when QUERY_UNDERSTANDING is on) turns the query's own words into pre-applied, visible, removable filters, reported under `query_understanding` with a replayable `param` per filter. Send `off` once the caller manages the filters itself, or the server re-adds the filter the user just removed.
